notice: Test build. The repair steps are unverified drafts and were not checked by a mechanic.

question.en: What kind of bike is it?
question.de: Was für ein Fahrrad ist es?

question.en: Does your bike have a motor?
Look at the rear wheel. Which picture looks like your bike?
question.de: Schau dir das Hinterrad an. Welches Bild sieht aus wie dein Fahrrad?

derailleur.en: Several sprockets, and a part below them that guides the chain
derailleur.de: Mehrere Ritzel und darunter ein Teil, das die Kette führt

hub_gear.en: One sprocket, and a thick hub in the middle of the wheel
hub_gear.de: Ein Ritzel und eine dicke Nabe in der Mitte des Rads

gearbox.en: One sprocket, and a box at the pedals
gearbox.de: Ein Ritzel und ein Kasten an den Pedalen

single_speed.en: One sprocket, and no way to change gear

facts.note: Only asked when drive.gear_type is derailleur, because conditions test it after the gear type.

question.en: Follow the shifter on the right of the handlebar. What connects it to the rear gears?
question.de: Folge dem Schalthebel rechts am Lenker. Was verbindet ihn mit der hinteren Schaltung?

mechanical.en: A thin cable in a housing
mechanical.de: Ein dünner Zug in einer Hülle

electronic.en: A wire with a plug, or no wire at all
electronic.de: Ein Kabel mit Stecker, oder gar kein Kabel

facts.note: Low-normal is also sold as rapid rise. Never asked, because a beginner cannot tell. Known from the bike's parts list, a partner, or the derailleur model. Unknown is treated as standard.

The heads of the limit and B screws. Never asked: it only picks the tool. Known from the bike's parts list or the derailleur model; when unknown, the tools screen shows both tools and how to tell them apart.
Detail fact. Never asked. Used in text when known.
Detail fact, for example the model printed on the derailleur. Never asked. Used in text when known.

choices.question: How will you hold the bike while you work?

options.label: In a work stand
options.note: The easiest way. The rear wheel turns freely and the bike cannot fall.
options.warning: Heavy bikes, such as e-bikes, can be too heavy for a small stand. Check the stand's maximum load.

options.label: Hanging from a hook or a rope
options.note: The rear wheel hangs free, so you can turn the pedals by hand.
options.warning: The hook or rope must carry the whole bike. A heavy bike can fall and hurt you.

options.label: Upside down, on saddle and handlebar
options.note: Needs no tools. The rear wheel turns freely.
options.warning: Turning a heavy bike over can hurt you. Ask someone to help.

options.label: On its wheels, and test with short rides
options.note: Needs no tools, but takes longer. You adjust while the bike stands and test by riding.

states.description: The bike is clamped in a work stand.
states.put_back: Take the bike out of the stand.

states.description: The bike hangs from a hook or a rope.
The bike stands upside down on its saddle and handlebar.
states.put_back: Turn the bike back onto its wheels.

tools.name: Strong hook or rope that can carry the bike

substitutes.name: Bike multi-tool with a small cross-head bit
Bike multi-tool with small hex keys

tool_sets.name: A tool for the small screws on the rear derailleur
tool_sets.tell_apart: Look at the small screws on the back of the rear derailleur. A cross in the screw head needs the screwdriver. A six-sided hole needs a hex key.

inspections.title: Look at the rear derailleur
inspections.text: Stand behind the bike and look at the rear derailleur, the part below the sprockets that guides the chain.

states.label: It hangs straight down, in line with the sprockets
states.meaning: The derailleur does not look bent.

states.label: It leans towards the spokes, or looks twisted
states.meaning: The derailleur or the part that holds it may be bent.

inspections.title: Find the barrel adjuster
inspections.text: Find the barrel adjuster: a small ribbed knob on the gear cable. Look where the cable enters the derailleur, then where it leaves the right shifter.

states.label: It is at the derailleur
states.meaning: The cable tension can be set at the derailleur.

states.label: It is at the shifter, or on the cable
states.meaning: The cable tension can be set there. It works the same way.

states.label: I cannot find one
states.meaning: This bike may have no barrel adjuster.

inspections.title: Look at the chain
inspections.text: Look at the chain below the pedals. Turn the pedals backwards slowly to see all of it.

states.label: Clean, with a thin film of oil
Dry, rusty, or it squeaks
states.meaning: The chain needs cleaning and oil. If the gears still shift badly afterwards, check again.

states.label: Black and gritty
states.meaning: The chain needs cleaning and oil. If the gears still shift badly afterwards, check again.

inspections.title: Test ride the gears
inspections.text: Ride slowly on a quiet, flat path. Use only the right shifter and change one gear at a time, all the way up and down.

states.label: Slow or rattling when shifting to easier gears
states.meaning: The chain is slow to climb to the bigger sprockets, the easier gears.

states.label: Slow or rattling when shifting to harder gears
states.meaning: The chain is slow to drop to the smaller sprockets, the harder gears.

states.label: Every gear changes quickly and runs quietly

shop.tell: The rear gears shift slowly or noisily. Please adjust the rear derailleur and check the gear cable.
The chain is dry, dirty or rusty. Please clean and oil it, and check it for wear.
The rear gears do not work as they should. Please check the rear derailleur, the part that holds it, and the gear cable.

steps.title: Clamp the bike in the stand
steps.text: Clamp the seat post in the stand so the rear wheel hangs free. With a heavy bike, ask someone to help you lift it.

animation.caption: Close the clamp around the seat post

steps.title: Hang the bike up
steps.text: Hang the bike by the front of its saddle from a strong hook or rope, so the rear wheel is off the ground, and check that it hangs firmly before you let go. Never use thin string or a coat hook: it can break, and the bike falls.

animation.amount: until the rear wheel is off the ground
animation.caption: Lift the rear of the bike onto the hook

steps.title: Turn the bike over
steps.text: Lay a soft mat on the floor and turn the bike over onto its saddle and handlebar. With a heavy bike, ask someone to help.

animation.caption: Turn the bike over onto the mat

steps.title: Take the bike out of the stand
steps.text: Hold the bike, open the stand clamp and put the bike on its wheels. With a heavy bike, ask someone to help.

animation.caption: Open the clamp while you hold the bike

steps.title: Take the bike down
steps.text: Hold the bike, lift it off the hook or rope and put the rear wheel on the ground.

animation.amount: until the rear wheel is on the ground
animation.caption: Lift the bike off and set it down

steps.title: Turn the bike back over
steps.text: Turn the bike back onto its wheels. With a heavy bike, ask someone to help.

animation.caption: Turn the bike back onto its wheels

steps.title: Park the bike
steps.text: Put the bike on its kickstand, or lean it against a wall at the saddle and rear wheel, with the gears facing you. Never lean it on the handlebar: it can turn, and the bike falls.

steps.title: Shift to the hardest gear
steps.text: Turn the pedals forward by hand and use the right shifter until the chain sits on the smallest sprocket, the hardest gear.

steps.title: Shift to the easiest gear
steps.text: Turn the pedals slowly by hand and shift one gear at a time until the chain sits on the largest sprocket, the easiest gear.

animation.caption: Shift one gear at a time

steps.title: Set the cable tension
steps.text: Turn the pedals by hand and shift one gear at a time, through all gears and back. Watch the chain.

buttons.label: Slow or noisy shifting to easier gears
buttons.text: The cable is too loose. Unscrew the barrel adjuster a quarter turn, then shift again. Never unscrew it all the way out.

solution.caption: Unscrew the barrel adjuster a quarter turn

buttons.label: Slow or noisy shifting to harder gears
buttons.text: The cable is too tight. Screw in the barrel adjuster a quarter turn, then shift again. If four turns do not help, a shop can check the cable.

solution.caption: Screw in the barrel adjuster a quarter turn

buttons.label: Every shift is quick and quiet

steps.title: Test every gear
steps.text: Turn the pedals and shift through every gear, from the hardest to the easiest and back. Watch and listen.

details.text: Your bike has {drive.rear_speeds} gears at the rear.

buttons.label: Every gear runs quietly
It rattles or jumps in some gears
buttons.text: Go back to the cable step and adjust as it says, then shift through again. If it does not get better, a shop can check the cable.

buttons.label: The chain falls off, or touches the spokes

exit.text: Do not ride: the chain can catch in the spokes and lock the wheel. Put the bike back on its wheels and take it to a shop.

steps.title: Ride into the hardest gear
steps.text: Ride slowly on a quiet path and shift into the hardest gear, the smallest sprocket. Stop, and park the bike as before.

steps.title: Ride into the easiest gear
steps.text: Ride slowly and shift one gear at a time into the easiest gear, the largest sprocket. Stop, and park the bike as before.

steps.title: Set the cable tension on short rides
steps.text: Ride slowly and shift one gear at a time, through all gears and back. Stop and park the bike before you turn anything.

buttons.label: Slow or noisy shifting to easier gears
buttons.text: The cable is too loose. Park the bike, unscrew the barrel adjuster a quarter turn, then ride and shift again. Never unscrew it all the way out.

solution.caption: Unscrew the barrel adjuster a quarter turn

buttons.label: Slow or noisy shifting to harder gears
buttons.text: The cable is too tight. Park the bike, screw in the barrel adjuster a quarter turn, then ride and shift again. If four turns do not help, a shop can check the cable.

solution.caption: Screw in the barrel adjuster a quarter turn

buttons.label: Every shift is quick and quiet

steps.title: Test every gear on a ride
steps.text: Ride once more and shift through every gear, from the hardest to the easiest and back. Watch and listen.

details.text: Your bike has {drive.rear_speeds} gears at the rear.

buttons.label: Every gear runs quietly
It rattles or jumps in some gears
buttons.text: Park the bike, go back to the cable step and adjust as it says, then ride again. If it does not get better, a shop can check the cable.

buttons.label: The chain falls off, or touches the spokes

exit.text: Stop riding: the chain can catch in the spokes and lock the wheel. Push the bike to a shop.

steps.title: Check the inner limit (L screw)
steps.text: Push the rear derailleur by hand towards the spokes, as far as it goes. Look from behind: where does the upper of its two small toothed wheels stop? You turn the screws with the small screwdriver or hex key.

animation.caption: Push the derailleur in by hand

buttons.label: In line with the largest sprocket
buttons.text: The L screw is set. Let go of the derailleur.

buttons.label: Past the largest sprocket, towards the spokes
buttons.block: Do not ride like this: the chain can fall into the spokes. Screw in the screw marked L a quarter turn, then push and look again.

solution.caption: Screw in the L screw a quarter turn

buttons.label: It stops before the largest sprocket
buttons.text: The chain may not reach the largest sprocket. Unscrew the screw marked L a quarter turn, then push and look again.

solution.caption: Unscrew the L screw a quarter turn

steps.title: Check the outer limit (H screw)
steps.text: Look from directly behind the bike at the upper of the two small toothed wheels on the derailleur. Where is it, compared with the smallest sprocket? You turn the screws with the small screwdriver or hex key.

buttons.label: In line with the smallest sprocket
buttons.text: The H screw is set. Nothing to change.

buttons.label: Further in, towards the spokes
buttons.text: Unscrew the screw marked H a quarter turn at a time, until the wheel is in line with the sprocket. If it does not move, stop turning: the cable holds it, and a later step sets the cable.

solution.caption: Unscrew the H screw a quarter turn

buttons.label: Further out, away from the spokes
buttons.block: The chain could fall off the outside and jam. Screw in the screw marked H a quarter turn at a time, until the wheel is in line with the sprocket.

solution.caption: Screw in the H screw a quarter turn

steps.title: Check the gap to the sprockets
steps.text: Keep the chain on the largest sprocket. Look from the side at the gap between the upper toothed wheel of the derailleur and the sprocket. You turn the screws with the small screwdriver or hex key.

buttons.label: A small gap, the teeth do not touch
buttons.text: The gap is fine. The manual for {drive.rear_derailleur_model|your derailleur} gives the exact gap, if you want to check it.

buttons.label: The wheel touches the sprocket, or almost
buttons.text: Screw in the B screw, at the back of the derailleur, a little at a time until there is a small gap.

solution.caption: Screw in the B screw a little

buttons.label: A big gap, and shifting here was slow
buttons.text: Unscrew the B screw a little at a time, until the gap is small but the teeth do not touch.

solution.caption: Unscrew the B screw a little
